case_title: GANGA SINGH v. STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH
evidence_type: eyewitness, circumstantial, medical, recovery, dying declaration
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted on the ground that sexual intercourse was with the consent of the prosecutrix
neutral_facts: The accused was prosecuted for rape. The prosecution alleged that the accused committed rape on the prosecutrix. The prosecutrix immediately after returning home narrated the incident to her mother-in-law. One day after the incident, when her husband returned home, she lodged an FIR. The medical report did not give a definite opinion on whether she suffered sexual intercourse, but the FSL report confirmed spots of semen and spermatozoa on her petticoat. The trial court acquitted the accused on the ground that sexual intercourse was with the consent of the prosecutrix. The High Court convicted the accused. The prosecutrix stated that the accused fell her down, covered her mouth, restricted her hands, and committed rape. The FIR and evidence of the prosecutrix's mother-in-law corroborated her statement. The FSL report confirmed sexual intercourse. The accused did not present a defense of consent and claimed he was falsely implicated due to a quarrel with the prosecutrix's husband, but this defense was not supported by evidence.
